spec.description: Download counts for your Docker Hub and GHCR images over the dashboard time range, grouped per package, with package and collector views. The counts are requests, not people or finished downloads, and on GHCR an automated manifest read counts too.

spec.title: Package downloads in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Every tracked package with its downloads in the dashboard time range, largest first, in a list that scrolls. Select a column heading to sort by it, and the rows add up to the Downloads tile on the Overview. Docker Hub and GHCR are added together unless Split by registry is on, which gives each registry its own row. A package tracked for only part of the range counts from its first read.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (round(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m]))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

spec.title: Downloads of the top 10 packages
spec.description: New downloads of the 10 packages with the most downloads in the dashboard time range, stacked in their own colours. Package downloads above lists every package, since the colours of more packages run together, and with Split by registry on the 10 are pairs of a package and a registry. A bar spans an hour on a day or less, 6 hours on a week, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months. A bar below zero means a registry restated its total lower, and a GHCR manifest read counts as a download.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(((sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__interval:1m]))) and on (owner, repo${split}) topk(10, sum by (owner, repo${split}) (round(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] @ ${__to:date:seconds}))))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ") and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Downloads in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Downloads across the selected packages and registries in the dashboard time range, whose length the title names, and the rows of Package downloads on the Packages tab add up to it. These are request counts as each registry reports them, so automated reads count too, and a registry that restates its total lower reduces the number. No downloads yet means no package has two reads in the range.

spec.expr: sum(round(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])))

spec.title: Change over ${spanthe} ${spanunit}
spec.description: The difference in downloads compared with ${spanthe:text} ${spanunit:text} before. It is the downloads of the dashboard time range minus those of the span of the same length that ends where the range starts. It keeps the text colour. A rise with no release behind it usually means an automated reader started polling, and No earlier range yet means the counts do not reach back that far.

spec.expr: sum(round(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])))

sum(round(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] offset $__range))) and (count(last_over_time((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"} offset $__range))[1d:1h] offset $__range)) > 0)

spec.title: Growth over ${spanthe} ${spanunit}
spec.description: The change in percent compared with ${spanthe:text} ${spanunit:text} before. It sets the downloads of the dashboard time range against those of the span of the same length that ends where the range starts. It is green from 0 up, yellow from -20 to 0 and red below -20. No earlier downloads means the counts do not reach back that far, or the earlier span counted no downloads, as on ranges of a few hours at the default hourly check.

spec.title: Recent pushes
spec.description: The 3 GHCR packages pushed most recently, newest first, from the "Last published" time each package page shows. Every push moves it, signatures, attestations and branch tags included, so a push is not always a release. Docker Hub publishes no push time, so only GHCR packages are listed. No pushes yet means no package page stated a time.

spec.expr: topk(3, max by (owner, repo) (registrystats_image_last_pushed_timestamp_seconds{registry="ghcr",repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner"})) * 1000

spec.title: Not pulled in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Packages whose count did not change at all over the dashboard time range, with their total, shown only while there is one. A package here has no readers, not even automated ones, so check a long range such as 30 days before you retire one. A count a registry restated lower is a change and keeps its package off the list, and a package appears only once every registry it is on reported it before the range began. Split by registry gives each registry its own row.

spec.title: Checks passed and failed
spec.description: Checks per registry across the selected collectors: passed in blue for Docker Hub and purple for GHCR, failed stacked on top in red and orange. A bar spans an hour on a day or less, 6 hours on a week, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months, and the legend total adds up the bars. Each collector checks once an hour at the default interval, so no bar means no check finished, and a check at either edge of the range can fall outside the bars. A failed check lost a whole listing or most of its package reads, so any red or orange bar is worth a look at the container log.

spec.expr: (label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collects_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))) - round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))), "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

(label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))) > 0, "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Check duration
spec.description: How long a full check of both registries takes, in minutes, as the median and the 95th percentile of the checks in each point's span. A span is an hour on a day or less, 6 hours on a week, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months. GHCR pages are spaced 2 to 5 seconds apart and Docker Hub requests half a second apart, so the time grows with the number of images. A climb with no new images means slower or retried requests.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (increase(registrystats_collect_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job"}[$__interval]))) / 60 and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (increase(registrystats_collect_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job"}[$__interval]))) / 60 and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Counts that went down in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Packages whose count is now below its highest value in the dashboard time range, with how far it fell, per registry. A registry restating its total, or a page read that returned a wrong number, causes this, and the download figures of the range are lower by that much. The shipped alert RegistryStatsPullCountRegressed fires on a fall within 2 days. No count went down means every count kept its high.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(max by (owner, repo, registry) (max_over_time(registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}[$__range]) - registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}) > 0, "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

defaults.noValue: No count went down in this range

spec.title: Memory
spec.description: Resident memory of each registry-stats process over the dashboard time range. It grows with the number of images tracked and stays flat between checks, so a steady climb across days points at a leak.

spec.expr: max by (instance) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job"})

spec.title: Collector not reporting
spec.description: A registry-stats scrape target your Prometheus server has failed to scrape for 15 minutes, by its instance, or No collector when the scrape job registry-stats has had no target for 15 minutes. It shows while the shipped alert RegistryStatsTargetDown or RegistryStatsTargetAbsent fires, as Not scraped where the alert names no instance, or checks their conditions itself where those rules are not loaded. Like them it needs the scrape job to be called registry-stats, and every other figure is stale until a collector reports again, so check the container and your scrape target.

spec.expr: label_replace(max by (instance) (ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsTargetDown", alertstate="firing"}), "instance", "Not scraped", "instance", "") or label_replace(max(ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsTargetAbsent", alertstate="firing"}), "instance", "No collector", "", "") or ((max by (instance) (count_over_time((up{job="registry-stats"} == 0)[16m:1m]) > 15) or label_replace(count_over_time(absent(up{job="registry-stats"})[16m:1m]) > 15, "instance", "No collector", "", "")) unless on () (count(max_over_time(ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsTargetDown"}[15m])) or count(max_over_time(ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsTargetAbsent"}[15m]))))

spec.title: Checks stalled
spec.description: A collector that has finished no check for 6 hours while it is still scraped, by its instance. It shows while the shipped alert RegistryStatsCollectStalled fires, or checks the same condition itself where that rule is not loaded. The collector keeps serving its last counts, so read its container log. In one-shot mode, with POLL_INTERVAL_HOURS at 0, this tile always shows.

spec.expr: max by (instance) (ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsCollectStalled", alertstate="firing"}) or (((min_over_time((sum by (job, instance) (increase(registrystats_collects_total[15m])) == bool 0)[6h1m:1m]) == 1) and on (job, instance) (count_over_time((sum by (job, instance) (increase(registrystats_collects_total[15m])) == bool 0)[6h1m:1m]) > 360)) unless on () count(max_over_time(ALERTS{alertname="RegistryStatsCollectStalled"}[6h])))

spec.title: Checks failing
spec.description: A registry whose checks have kept failing for 3 hours, with its failed checks of those 3 hours, so its packages are missing from the counts or out of date. It shows while the shipped alert RegistryStatsSourceDegraded fires, or checks the same condition itself where that rule is not loaded: a check failed within every 90 minutes for 3 hours. One failed check in a short registry outage does not show, and a registry that cannot be read at all lights Registry data stale first, after 2 hours. Read the container log for the owner and the cause, such as a rate limit or a changed page, and wait out an outage of the registry itself.

spec.title: Registry data stale
spec.description: Time since a registry was last read successfully, shown once it passes 2 hours, for the collector read longest ago. The 2 hours assume the default hourly check. No shipped alert reads this age, so check Checks failing and the container log for the cause.

spec.title: Counts that went down
spec.description: How many packages, counted per registry, have held a count below its highest value of the last 2 days for 30 minutes. It shows while the shipped alert RegistryStatsPullCountRegressed fires, or checks the same condition itself where that rule is not loaded.
